sentences.zh: 曹志

translations.literal: Cao Zhi
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi

sentences.zh: 曹志，字允恭，譙國譙人，魏陳思王植之孽子也。

translations.literal: Cao Zhi, style Yungong, was a man of Qiao in the Principality of Qiao, and was a natural son of Cao Zhi, Prince Si of Chen of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi, courtesy name Yungong, came from Qiao in the Principality of Qiao. He was a natural son of Prince Si of Chen, Cao Zhi, of Wei—the celebrated poet-prince whose name is written with the same characters as his son's.

sentences.zh: 少好學，以才行稱，夷簡有大度，兼善騎射。

translations.literal: In youth he loved study, was acclaimed for talent and conduct, was equable and simple and had great capacity, and was also skilled in riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he loved learning and was praised for talent and character: unassuming, broad-minded, and also a capable horseman and archer.

sentences.zh: 植曰：「此保家主也。

translations.literal: His father said, "This is one who will preserve the family."
translations.idiomatic: His father said, "This is a son who will keep our house secure."

sentences.zh: 」立以為嗣。

translations.literal: He established him as heir.
translations.idiomatic: He named him heir.

sentences.zh: 後改封濟北王。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to be Prince of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently given the princely title of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 武帝為撫軍將軍，迎陳留王於鄴，志夜謁見，帝與語，自暮達旦，甚奇之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was General Who Comforts the Army and welcomed the Prince of Chenliu at Ye, Cao Zhi by night requested an audience; the Emperor conversed with him from dusk to dawn and greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: While Sima Yan still held the post of General Who Comforts the Army and had gone to Ye to welcome the Prince of Chenliu, Cao Zhi sought a nighttime audience. The two talked from dusk until dawn, and Sima Yan was deeply struck by him.

sentences.zh: 及帝受禪，降為鄄城縣公。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the abdication, he was demoted to Duke of Juancheng county.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Yan accepted the abdication and ascended the throne, Cao Zhi was reduced in rank to Duke of Juancheng county.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔在前世，雖曆運迭興，至於先代苗裔，傳祚不替，或列籓九服，式序王官。

translations.literal: An edict stated, "In former ages, though the dynastic fortune rose and fell in turn, as to the descendants of former dynasties, their transmission of the mandate was not cut off; some were arrayed as fiefs throughout the Nine Domains, and thereby took their place among the king's officials.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "In antiquity, even as one mandate succeeded another, the bloodlines of earlier houses often kept their altars—some enfeoffed across the submissive regions, others enrolled in the ruler's bureaucracy."

sentences.zh: 選眾命賢，惟德是與，蓋至公之道也。

translations.literal: Choosing from the many and appointing the worthy, giving place only to virtue—this is the way of utmost fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Choosing worthies wherever they are found and favouring only virtue—that is the path of perfect impartiality.

sentences.zh: 魏氏諸王公養德藏器，壅滯曠久，前雖有詔，當須簡授，而自頃眾職少缺，未得式敘。

translations.literal: The various princes and dukes of the Wei house cultivated virtue and concealed their talents, blocked and stagnant for long; though earlier there had been an edict that they must await selection and appointment, yet recently many posts have stood short-handed, and they have not yet been duly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and dukes of Wei have long kept their talents hidden and gone unused. Though an edict already called for their careful selection and posting, many offices have lately stood vacant, and proper placement has yet to come.

sentences.zh: 前濟北王曹志履德清純，才高行潔，好古博物，為魏宗英，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The former Prince of Jibei, Cao Zhi, treads virtue in purity and refinement, his talent is lofty and his conduct immaculate, he loves antiquity and is broadly learned in things, and is an outstanding one of the Wei imperial house; We greatly commend him.
translations.idiomatic: As for the former Prince of Jibei, Cao Zhi, he practices virtue with singular purity, combines high talent with spotless conduct, and delights in antiquity and wide learning—an ornament of the Wei imperial clan. We hold him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 其以志為樂平太守。

translations.literal: Let Cao Zhi be made Administrator of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi is hereby appointed Administrator of Leping.

sentences.zh: 」志在郡上書，以為宜尊儒重道，請為博士置吏卒。

translations.literal: Cao Zhi, while in the commandery, submitted a memorial holding that one should honour Confucian learning and esteem the Way, and he requested that clerks and guards be assigned to the erudits.
translations.idiomatic: While governing the commandery Cao Zhi submitted a memorial arguing that Confucian learning and the Way deserved renewed emphasis, and asking that the doctoral scholars be allotted clerks and guard details.

sentences.zh: 遷章武、趙郡太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Administrator of Zhangwu and of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to serve as Administrator of Zhangwu and then of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 雖累郡職，不以政事為意，晝則遊獵，夜誦《詩》《書》，以聲色自娛，當時見者未能審其量也。

translations.literal: Though he successively held commandery posts, he did not take administration to heart; by day he roamed and hunted, by night he recited the Odes and the Documents, and amused himself with music and beauty; those who saw him at the time could not yet fathom his measure.
translations.idiomatic: Though he served in several commanderies, he showed little zeal for paperwork—hunting by day, reading the Classic of Poetry and the Documents by night, finding his ease in music and company. Contemporaries who watched him could not yet read the depth of the man.

sentences.zh: 咸甯初，詔曰：「鄄城公曹志，篤行履素，達學通識，宜在儒林，以弘胄子之教。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianning, an edict stated, "Duke of Juancheng Cao Zhi, in conduct sincere and in practice plain, broadly learned and comprehensively versed, should stand within Confucian scholars, so as to enlarge the instruction of the scions.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianning era an edict declared: "Duke of Juancheng Cao Zhi combines steady character with plain living, wide scholarship with sound judgment. He belongs among the literati who may enlarge the education of the heir-apparents."

sentences.zh: 其以志為散騎常侍、國子博士。

translations.literal: Let Cao Zhi be made Palace Attendant-in-ordinary and erudit of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint him Palace Attendant-in-ordinary and Doctoral Lecturer at the National University.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘗閱《六代論》，問志曰：「是卿先王所作邪？

translations.literal: The Emperor once inspected the Treatise on the Six Dynasties and asked Cao Zhi, "Was this written by your former prince?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan once read the Treatise on the Six Dynasties and asked Cao Zhi, "Did your royal father compose this?"

sentences.zh: 」志對曰：「先王有手所作目錄，請歸尋按。

translations.literal: Cao Zhi replied, "My former prince had a catalogue written in his own hand; I beg leave to return and search according to it."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi answered, "My father kept a catalogue in his own hand. Allow me to go home and check it against that record."

sentences.zh: 」還奏曰：「按錄無此。

translations.literal: Having returned he reported, "According to the catalogue there is no such item."
translations.idiomatic: When he came back he reported, "The catalogue contains no such title."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「誰作？

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Who composed it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Who did write it, then?"

sentences.zh: 」志曰：「以臣所聞，是臣族父冏所作。

translations.literal: Cao Zhi said, "According to what your servant has heard, it was composed by your servant's clansman Cao Jiong."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi said, "From what I have learned, it was the work of my kinsman Cao Jiong."

sentences.zh: 以先王文高名著，欲令書傳於後，是以假託。

translations.literal: Because my former prince's writing was lofty and his fame eminent, he wished the book to be transmitted to later generations, and therefore falsely attributed it.
translations.idiomatic: Because his own father's literary name stood so high, Cao Jiong hoped the essay would endure under that name, and therefore published it under borrowed authorship.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「古來亦多有是。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "From antiquity there have also been many such cases."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Such things are common enough in the record of the past."

sentences.zh: 」顧謂公卿曰：「父子證明，足以為審。

translations.literal: Turning, he said to the dukes and ministers, "Father and son have vouched for the truth; this suffices to be deemed certain."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to the assembled nobles he added, "Father and son have attested to the facts; that is proof enough."

sentences.zh: 自今已後，可無復疑。」

translations.literal: From today onward, there need be no further doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth no one should doubt the matter.

sentences.zh: 後遷祭酒。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently promoted to Libationer of the National University.

sentences.zh: 齊王攸將之國，下太常議崇錫文物。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi, Sima You, was about to go to his state; an order was issued to the Chamberlain of Ceremonies to deliberate on the grants of honours and implements.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Sima You of Qi was preparing to leave for his princely fief, the court referred the matter to the Chamberlain of Ceremonies to decide what honours and ritual gear should be granted.

sentences.zh: 時博士秦秀等以為齊王宜內匡朝政，不可之籓。

translations.literal: At the time Erudits such as Qin Xiu held that the Prince of Qi ought to aid the court government from within and ought not go to a fief.
translations.idiomatic: Erudits led by Qin Xiu argued that the Prince of Qi should stay at court to steady the government rather than be sent out to a regional apanage.

sentences.zh: 志又常恨其父不得志于魏，因愴然歎曰：「安有如此之才，如此之親，不得樹本助化，而遠出海隅？

translations.literal: Cao Zhi, moreover, often resented that his father had not fulfilled his ambitions in Wei, and therefore sighed mournfully, saying, "How can there be such talent and such closeness of kin, yet be unable to plant one's roots and assist in transformation, and instead be sent far off to the sea's corner?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi still nursed the old wound of his father's thwarted career in Wei, and once said in bitter sorrow, "When a man wields such talent and bears such closeness to the throne, how can he be denied a place at the capital to nourish the state, and instead be banished to some remote corner by the sea?"

sentences.zh: 晉朝之隆，其殆乎哉！

translations.literal: The prosperity of the house of Jin—will it not be imperilled!
translations.idiomatic: If this is the court's policy, how can the Jin dynasty hope to flourish?

sentences.zh: 」乃奏議曰：「伏聞大司馬齊王當出籓東夏，備物盡禮，同之二伯。

translations.literal: He then presented a memorial stating, "I have heard that the Grand Marshal, Prince of Qi, is to leave for his fief in the eastern summer regions, with full provision of things and observance of rites, equated with the Two Elder Lords.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he drafted a memorial: "I have learned that the Grand Marshal, Prince of Qi, is ordered to his fief in the east with full panoply of gifts and rites, his dignity equated with the two great bulwarks of Zhou."

sentences.zh: 今陛下為聖君，稷、契為賢臣，內有魯、衛之親，外有齊、晉之輔，坐而守安，此萬世之基也。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty is a sage ruler, Ji and Xie are worthy ministers, within there is the closeness of Lu and Wei, without there is the support of Qi and Jin; sitting still and guarding tranquillity—this is the foundation for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty reigns as a true sage; ministers of the caliber of Ji and Xie serve at your side. Within the palace you have princes as close as the ancient dukes of Lu and Wei; beyond it you have bulwarks like Qi and Jin. To preserve stability from the throne is to lay a foundation meant to last for ages.

sentences.zh: 古之夾輔王室，同姓則周公其人也，異姓則太公其人也，皆身在內，五世反葬。

translations.literal: Of old those who flanked and aided the royal house—the same surname had the Duke of Zhou as their man, a different surname had the Grand Duke as their man; both were personally within the court, and though five generations passed they returned for burial.
translations.idiomatic: History's model guardians of the throne were men like the Duke of Zhou for royal kin or the Grand Duke Wang for outsiders—both kept their persons at the capital and, even after generations of service abroad, were brought home to lie with their ancestors.

sentences.zh: 後雖有五霸代興，桓、文譎主，下有請隧之僭，上有九錫之禮，終於譎而不正，驗於尾大不掉，豈與召公之歌《棠棣》，周詩之詠《鴟鴞》同日論哉！

translations.literal: Afterward, though the Five Lords Protector arose in succession, Huan and Wen were crafty masters; below there was the arrogance of requesting a tunnel rite, above there was the ritual of the Nine Bestowals; in the end crafty and not orthodox, verified by tails too large to wag—how could it be discussed on the same day as the Duke of Shao's song Elder Brothers or the Zhou odes' recitation of Owl!
translations.idiomatic: Later ages produced the so-called Five Hegemons: rulers like Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin who ruled by cunning. Their vassals pressed for rites reserved for a king—tunnel entrances to their tombs—while the hegemons themselves pressed upward for the "nine ritual gifts" meant to signal abdication. Such power never rested on legitimate authority; history shows it always ends with a vassal too bloated for his lord to control. How can that arrogant rising of ministers be mentioned in the same breath as the Duke of Shao's hymn to brotherhood in The Elder Brothers, or the loyal reproof voiced in the ode The Owl?

sentences.zh: 今聖朝創業之始，始之不諒，後事難工。

translations.literal: Now at the beginning of the holy dynasty's founding of enterprise, if the beginning is not made trustworthy, later tasks will be hard to complete.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of a dynasty like ours, what is not settled honestly at the outset can scarcely be put right later.

sentences.zh: 幹植不強，枝葉不茂；

translations.literal: If the trunk is not strong, branches and leaves will not flourish;
translations.idiomatic: A weak trunk cannot bear luxuriant branches.

sentences.zh: 骨骾不存，皮膚不充。

translations.literal: If bones and marrow do not endure, skin and flesh will not be full.
translations.idiomatic: Without bone and marrow beneath, the skin has nothing to rest on.

sentences.zh: 自羲皇以來，豈是一姓之獨有！

translations.literal: Since the time of Emperor Xi, has it ever been the monopoly of one surname!
translations.idiomatic: From the age of the legendary rulers onward, no single clan has ever monopolized the realm forever.

sentences.zh: 欲結其心者，當有磐石之固。

translations.literal: Those who wish to bind men's hearts must have firmness like a standing rock.
translations.idiomatic: He who would win men's loyalty must offer them a bulwark as immovable as stone.

sentences.zh: 夫欲享萬世之利者，當與天下議之。

translations.literal: Those who wish to enjoy benefit for ten thousand generations must deliberate with All-under-Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He who seeks a blessing that lasts many lifetimes must consult the realm at large.

sentences.zh: 故天之聰明，自我人之聰明。

translations.literal: Therefore Heaven's keen hearing and clear vision is from our people's keen hearing and clear vision.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the wisdom attributed to Heaven is drawn from the wisdom of the human community itself.

sentences.zh: 秦、魏欲獨擅其威，而財得沒其身；

translations.literal: Qin and Wei wished monopolistically to grasp their awesomeness, and in the end only succeeded in destroying themselves;
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Wei tried to hoard all power in their own hands—and succeeded only in destroying themselves.

sentences.zh: 周、漢能分其利，而親疏為之用。

translations.literal: Zhou and Han were able to divide the benefit, and thereby kin and distant were employed for use.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Han shared their advantages with many hands and so turned both kinsmen and outsiders to account.

sentences.zh: 此自聖主之深慮，日月之所照。

translations.literal: This is from the sage ruler's deep planning, where sun and moon shine.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the far-sighted policy of wise sovereigns—plain as sunlight and moonlight.

sentences.zh: 事雖淺，當深謀之；

translations.literal: Though the matter is shallow, one should plan it deeply;
translations.idiomatic: Even a seemingly small matter calls for the deepest counsel.

sentences.zh: 言雖輕，當重思之。

translations.literal: Though the words are light, one should ponder them heavily.
translations.idiomatic: Even words spoken lightly deserve the most serious reflection.

sentences.zh: 志備位儒官，若言不及禮，是志寇竊。

translations.literal: Cao Zhi occupies a Confucian officer's place in name; if his words do not reach to ritual, then Cao Zhi is a robber-thief.
translations.idiomatic: I hold a merely nominal place among the ritual specialists; if what I say falls short of propriety, then I am no better than a thief dressed in scholar's robes.

sentences.zh: 知忠不言，議所不敢。

translations.literal: To know loyalty and not speak is what, in deliberation, I dare not.
translations.idiomatic: To see what duty requires and hold silence is something my conscience will not allow.

sentences.zh: 志以為當如博士等議。

translations.literal: Cao Zhi held that it should be as the erudits and others argued.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi believed the court should adopt the erudits' recommendation.

sentences.zh: 」議成當上，見其從弟高邑公嘉。

translations.literal: When the deliberation was finished and about to be submitted, he met his younger patrilateral cousin, Duke of Gaoyi, Cao Jia.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was ready to go up, he met his cousin Cao Jia, Duke of Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 嘉曰：「兄議甚切，百年之後必書晉史，目下將見責邪。

translations.literal: Cao Jia said, "Elder's argument is very cutting; after a hundred years it will surely be recorded in Jin history—will you presently be blamed?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jia warned him, "This memorial cuts deep. Historians will note it—but are you ready for the anger you will draw today?"

sentences.zh: 」帝覽議，大怒曰：「曹志尚不明吾心，況四海乎！

translations.literal: The Emperor reviewed the deliberation and greatly raged, saying, "If Cao Zhi still does not understand Our heart, how much less All-under-Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor read the memorial his wrath flared. "If Cao Zhi cannot read my mind," he cried, "what hope is there for the four seas?"

sentences.zh: 」以議者不指答所問，橫造異論，策免太常鄭默。

translations.literal: Because the debaters did not pointedly answer what was asked but sideways produced divergent discourse, by rescript he dismissed Chamberlain of Ceremonies Zheng Mo.
translations.idiomatic: On the grounds that the memorialists had strayed from the brief and stirred irrelevant controversy, he dismissed Zheng Mo from the chamberlainship by rescript.

sentences.zh: 於是有司奏收志等結罪，詔惟免志官，以公還第，其餘皆付廷尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the authorities reported memorializing to arrest Cao Zhi and others for conspiracy crimes; an edict solely removed Cao Zhi from office, sent him back to his mansion as duke, and the rest were all handed to the Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The bureaus then asked that Cao Zhi and his colleagues be seized on charges of conspiracy. The emperor would go no further than stripping Cao Zhi of office while letting him retire to his ducal mansion; the others he sent to the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 頃之，志復為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long, Cao Zhi was again Palace Attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Cao Zhi was restored to his former post as Palace Attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，居喪過禮，因此篤病，喜怒失常。

translations.literal: He encountered mourning for his mother; in observing mourning he exceeded the rites, and on that account fell seriously ill, joy and anger losing normality.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he mourned so extravagantly that he broke down in health; joy and anger thereafter slipped beyond his control.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，太常奏以惡諡。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died; the Chamberlain of Ceremonies submitted that an inauspicious posthumous name be given.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of the era; the Chamberlain of Ceremonies proposed withholding a favourable posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 崔褒歎曰：「魏顆不從亂，以病為亂故也。

translations.literal: Cui Bao sighed, saying, "Wei Ke did not follow a deranged command because illness was taken as the cause of disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Bao reminded them, "Wei Ke earned the posthumous epithet Steadfast precisely because he refused a father's insane order, knowing that illness—not defiance—had caused the confusion."

sentences.zh: 今諡曹志而諡其病，豈謂其病不為亂乎！

translations.literal: Now, in giving Cao Zhi a posthumous name and imputing his illness, do you mean that his illness was not disorder!
translations.idiomatic: To fix a cruel posthumous verdict on Cao Zhi by citing his mental collapse is to pretend his ailment was not the very sort of disorder that excused Wei Ke's father—not a fair reading of precedent at all.

sentences.zh: 」於是諡為定。

translations.literal: Thereupon his posthumous name was fixed as Ding.
translations.idiomatic: On that reasoning they settled on the posthumous name Ding (Steadfast).

sentences.zh: 庾峻

translations.literal: Yu Jun
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jun

sentences.zh: 庾峻，字山甫，潁川鄢陵人也。

translations.literal: Yu Jun, style Shanfu, was a man of Yanling in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jun, courtesy name Shanfu, came from Yanling in Yingchuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖乘，才學洽聞，漢司徒辟，有道征，皆不就。

translations.literal: His grandfather Cheng was talented and learned, broadly heard of; the Han Excellency over the Masses summoned him, and he was summoned on account of virtue, but in each case he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu Cheng combined wide learning with a celebrated reputation. The Han Excellency over the Masses called him to office and he was nominated as a man of high principle, yet he declined every appointment.

sentences.zh: 伯父嶷，中正簡素，仕魏為太僕。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Ni was unbiased and simple; he served Wei as Grand Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Yu Ni, chosen as a local merit assessor, was known for plain integrity; he rose under Wei to Grand Coachman.

sentences.zh: 父道，廉退貞固，養志不仕。

translations.literal: His father Dao was incorrupt, retiring, chaste and firm, nurturing his will and not taking office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu Dao lived modestly, withdrew from ambition, and kept such stern integrity that he never took office.

sentences.zh: 牛馬有踶齧者，恐傷人，不貨於市。

translations.literal: Regarding cows and horses that kick and bite, fearing they would harm people, he did not offer them for sale in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Dao refused to sell cattle or horses known to kick or bite, lest they injure buyers in the market.

sentences.zh: 及諸子貴，賜拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: When his various sons became honoured, he was granted appointment as Grand Palace Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Once his sons had risen to distinction, the court honoured him with the title of Grand Palace Grandee.

sentences.zh: 峻少好學，有才思。

translations.literal: Jun in youth loved study and had talent and ideas.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jun loved learning from boyhood and showed a ready wit.

sentences.zh: 嘗游京師，聞魏散騎常侍蘇林老疾在家，往候之。

translations.literal: He once travelled to the capital; hearing that Wei's Palace Attendant-in-ordinary Su Lin was old and ill at home, he went to inquire of him.
translations.idiomatic: During a visit to the capital he heard that the veteran scholar Su Lin lay ill at home, and he went to pay his respects.

sentences.zh: 林嘗就乘學，見峻流涕，良久曰：「尊祖高才而性退讓，慈和泛愛，清靜寡欲，不營當世，惟修德行而已。

translations.literal: Lin had once studied under Cheng; seeing Jun he wept and after a long while said, "Your honourable grandfather had lofty talent but a nature humble and yielding, kind and harmonious and broadly loving, pure and quiet with few desires, not scrambling for the present age—only cultivating virtue, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Su Lin had once studied under Yu Cheng. When he saw Yu Jun he wept and said after a long silence, "Your grandfather was a man of towering ability yet modest habits—kind, generous, quiet, and little interested in worldly gain. He cared only for cultivating character."

sentences.zh: 鄢陵舊五六萬戶，聞今裁有數百。

translations.literal: Yanling of old had fifty or sixty thousand households; I hear that now it is only a few hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling once counted fifty or sixty thousand households; today I hear there are only a few hundred left.

sentences.zh: 君二父孩抱經亂，獨至今日，尊伯為當世令器，君兄弟復俊茂，此尊祖積德之所由也。」

translations.literal: Your two fathers were infants in arms through the turmoil, yet alone have reached this day; your honourable uncle is a fine vessel of the age, you, brothers, again are outstanding—this is the reason from your honourable grandfather's accumulated virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Your father and uncle were only infants when the realm convulsed, yet they alone survived to this day. Your uncle is one of the age's chief talents, and you brothers are rising stars beside him—all of it fruit of the virtue your grandfather laid up.

sentences.zh: 曆郡功曹，舉計掾，州辟從事。

translations.literal: He passed through commandery headquarters clerk, was recommended as accounting aide, and was summoned by the province as retainer.
translations.idiomatic: He served as headquarters clerk in the commandery, was nominated as accounting officer, and the province summoned him as a staff retainer.

sentences.zh: 太常鄭袤見峻，大奇之，舉為博士。

translations.literal: Chamberlain of Ceremonies Zheng Mao saw Jun and greatly marvelled at him, recommending him as erudit.
translations.idiomatic: When Chamberlain Zheng Mao met Yu Jun he was so impressed that he nominated him for a doctorate.

sentences.zh: 時重《莊》《老》而輕《經》《史》，駿懼雅道陵遲，乃潛心儒典。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuangzi and Laozi were esteemed while the Classics and histories were slighted; Jun feared that the cultured Way would decline, and therefore immersed himself in Confucian canons.
translations.idiomatic: At court the Zhuangzi and Laozi were all the fashion while the Classics and histories languished. Fearing that the high culture of the Confucian tradition would fade, Yu Jun buried himself in the orthodox canon.

sentences.zh: 屬高貴鄉公幸太學，問《尚書》義于峻，峻援引師說，發明經旨，申暢疑滯，對答詳悉。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Gaoguixiang visited the Imperial Academy and asked Yu Jun for the meaning of the Documents, Jun cited masters' explanations, opened up the classic's purport, extended and cleared doubts and blocks, answering in detail and exhaustively.
translations.idiomatic: On the occasion of Duke Cao Mao's visit to the Imperial Academy, the young emperor quizzed Yu Jun on the Documents. Yu Jun drew on the glosses of the masters, unfolded the text layer by layer, and unraveled every knotty passage with patient clarity.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted Assistant in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 長安有大獄，久不決，拜峻侍御史，往斷之，朝野稱允。

translations.literal: Chang'an had a great case long unsettled; Jun was appointed Attendant Censor and sent to decide it; court and countryside praised it as fair.
translations.idiomatic: A major lawsuit had stalled for months in Chang'an; the court named Yu Jun Attendant Censor and sent him to settle it. Both capital and province praised the outcome as just.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，賜爵關中侯，遷司空長史，轉秘書監、御史中丞，拜侍中，加諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed with noble rank as Marquis Within the Passes, promoted Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works, transferred to Palace Library Supervisor and Palace Attendant Censor-in-chief, appointed Palace Attendant, and added Grand Counsellor of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yan mounted the throne he ennobled Yu Jun as Marquis Within the Passes, advanced him through chief clerk of the Ministry of Works to director of the Palace Library and censor-in-chief, then appointed him palace attendant with the added title of grand counsellor of the household.

sentences.zh: 常侍帝講《詩》，中庶子何劭論《風》《雅》正變之義，峻起難往反，四坐莫能屈之。

translations.literal: He regularly attended the Emperor's exposition of the Odes; Household Grandee He Shao debated the meaning of orthodoxy and change in Airs and Elegances; Jun rose and disputed back and forth, and none in the four seats could bend him.
translations.idiomatic: While attending Sima Yan's lectures on the Classic of Poetry, he crossed swords with Household Grandee He Shao over what counted as orthodox or declining lyrics in the Airs and Elegances; after several rounds of debate no one at table could break his argument.

sentences.zh: 是時風俗趣競，禮讓陵遲。

translations.literal: At that time custom hastened to rivalry and courtesy yielded to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Public manners had turned brutally competitive; deference and yielding were everywhere eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 峻上疏曰：

translations.literal: Yu Jun submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jun therefore submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 又疾世浮華，不修名實，著論以非之，文繁不載。

translations.literal: He also detested the world's flashiness and failure to cultivate name and reality; he wrote a treatise to criticize it—the text being abundant, it is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise loathed the age's love of display and neglect of substance, and composed a polemic against it—the editors omit the essay here on grounds of length.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，詔賜朝服一具、衣一襲、錢三十萬。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died; an edict bestowed one set of court robes, one suit of garments, and three hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of the Taishi era; the court sent one full set of court dress, a suit of clothes, and three hundred thousand cash for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 臨終，敕子瑉朝卒夕殯，幅巾布衣，葬勿擇日。

translations.literal: At life's end he instructed his son Min: bury at morning's death by evening's burial; with headcloth and plain clothes; for burial do not select a day.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he ordered his son Yu Min to bury him the same evening he died, with no imported finery—only hemp headcloth and plain robes—and without fussing over an auspicious burial day.

sentences.zh: 瑉奉遵遺命，斂以時服。

translations.literal: Min obeyed the testamentary command, dressing the corpse in timely garments.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Min followed those instructions to the letter, laying his father out only in the clothes of the season.

sentences.zh: 二子：瑉、敳。

translations.literal: Two sons: Min and Ai.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Yu Min and Yu Ai.

translations.literal: The transmitted line consists of an equals sign with no lexical gloss in the edition used here.
translations.idiomatic: The base text here reads only as an equals sign, probably a table-row artifact carried over from the edition.

sentences.zh: 子瑉

translations.literal: Son Min
translations.idiomatic: Yu Min

sentences.zh: =瑉字子琚。

translations.literal: = Min, style Ziju.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Min, courtesy name Ziju—the stray mark before his name is an edition artifact.

sentences.zh: 性淳和好學，行己忠恕。

translations.literal: His nature was pure, harmonious, and fond of study; in conducting himself he was loyal and forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: He was guileless, affable, devoted to learning, and governed himself with loyalty and tolerance.

sentences.zh: 少曆散騎常侍、本國中正、侍中，封長岑男。

translations.literal: In youth he passed through Palace Attendant-in-ordinary, impartial judge of his native state, Palace Attendant, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Changcen.
translations.idiomatic: While still young he rose through palace attendant-in-chief, local merit assessor for his princedom, palace attendant, and received the barony of Changcen.

sentences.zh: 懷帝之沒劉元海也，瑉從在平陽。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai fell to Liu Yuanhai, Min followed him in Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huai fell captive to Liu Yuan (Liu Yuanhai), Yu Min accompanied him to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 元海大會，因使帝行酒，瑉不勝悲憤，再拜上酒，因大號哭，賊惡之。

translations.literal: Yuanhai held a great gathering and thereupon made the Emperor pour wine; Min could not bear grief and rage, twice bowed and presented wine, then loudly wailed; the bandits detested him.
translations.idiomatic: At one of Liu Yuan's banquets the Jin emperor was forced to serve wine to the guests. Yu Min, unable to choke back grief, bowed twice as he presented the cup, then burst into open weeping. The rebels took an instant dislike to him.

sentences.zh: 會有告瑉及王儁等謀應劉琨者，元海因圖弑逆，瑉等並遇害。

translations.literal: Then there was one who reported that Min and Wang Jun and others plotted to respond to Liu Kun; Yuanhai thereupon plotted regicide; Min and the rest together met murder.
translations.idiomatic: When someone accused Yu Min, Wang Jun, and others of plotting to help Liu Kun, Liu Yuan seized the excuse to move against the emperor; Yu Min and his fellows were put to death.

sentences.zh: 初，洛陽之未陷也，瑉為侍中，直於省內，謂同僚許遐曰：「世路如此，禍難將及，吾當死乎此屋耳！

translations.literal: Earlier, when Luoyang had not yet fallen, Min was Palace Attendant, on duty within the ministry; he said to fellow official Xu Xia, "The age's roads are like this; calamity will arrive—I shall surely die in this chamber!"
translations.idiomatic: Before Luoyang fell, Yu Min was on duty as a palace attendant in the ministries. He once told his colleague Xu Xia, "The times have turned this vicious; disaster is at our door—I expect to die in this very hall!"

sentences.zh: 」及是，竟不免焉。

translations.literal: When it came to this, in the end he did not escape it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not escape the fate he foresaw.

sentences.zh: 太元末，追諡曰貞。

translations.literal: At the end of Taiyuan, posthumously his posthumous name was pronounced Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Taiyuan era the court posthumously honoured him with the name Zhen (Steadfast).

translations.literal: The transmitted line consists of an equals sign with no lexical gloss in the edition used here.
translations.idiomatic: The edition again inserts a lone equals sign, almost certainly a table-row artifact.

sentences.zh: 瑉弟敳

translations.literal: Yu Min's younger brother Yu Ai.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ai, younger brother of Yu Min.

sentences.zh: =敳字子嵩。

translations.literal: Yu Ai, style Zisong.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ai, courtesy name Zisong—the stray mark before his name is an edition artifact.

sentences.zh: 長不滿七尺，而腰帶十圍，雅有遠韻。

translations.literal: Though his height did not reach seven chi, his girdle spanned ten hand-breadths; he had refined, far-reaching charm.
translations.idiomatic: He stood under seven feet tall yet girded a waist ten spans round, carrying an air of distant, understated elegance.

sentences.zh: 為陳留相，未嘗以事嬰心，從容酣暢，寄通而已。

translations.literal: As Chancellor of Chenliu he never let affairs entangle his mind; he was leisurely, freely enjoying wine, and merely let things flow through him.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor of Chenliu he refused to let paperwork fret him—he drank deep, took life as it came, and let events pass like water.

sentences.zh: 處眾人中，居然獨立。

translations.literal: Among a crowd of people he stood as if alone.
translations.idiomatic: In a throng he seemed to stand apart, self-contained and untouchable.

sentences.zh: 嘗讀《老》《莊》，曰：「正與人意暗同。

translations.literal: Once, reading the Laozi and the Zhuangzi, he said, "They match what people feel in secret."
translations.idiomatic: Once, reading the 《Laozi》 and the 《Zhuangzi》, he remarked, "These texts voice exactly what most of us feel but never say aloud."

sentences.zh: 」太尉王衍雅重之。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant Wang Yan greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Wang Yan held him in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 敳見王室多難，終知嬰禍，乃著《意賦》以豁情，猶賈誼之《服鳥》也。

translations.literal: Seeing that the royal house faced many troubles, Yu Ai ultimately knew he would be caught in disaster; therefore he composed the Rhapsody on Intent to clear his feelings, like Jia Yi's Rhapsody on the Owl.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing endless peril closing in on the throne, Yu Ai knew calamity would find him too; he wrote the *Rhapsody on Intent* to steady his heart, much as Jia Yi once wrote the *Rhapsody on the Owl*.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：「至理歸於渾一兮，榮辱固亦同貫。

translations.literal: Its words say, "The utmost pattern returns to undivided oneness; glory and shame surely share one thread."
translations.idiomatic: The piece opens: "The highest truth folds back into primal unity; honour and disgrace run on the same string."

sentences.zh: 存亡既已均齊兮，正盡死復何歎。

translations.literal: Life and death are already levelled; why sigh again when righteousness is exhausted and death comes?
translations.idiomatic: Since life and death are already level, why lament once duty ends and death arrives?

sentences.zh: 物咸定于無初兮，俟時至而後驗。

translations.literal: All things are fixed from the beginning without origin; one waits until the time arrives and then it is verified.
translations.idiomatic: Every creature is set on its course before a beginning can be named; only when the appointed hour comes is the pattern plain.

sentences.zh: 若四節之素代兮，豈當今之得遠？

translations.literal: If the four seasons replace one another in due order, how can the present ever be kept distant?
translations.idiomatic: If spring, summer, autumn, and winter rotate in their proper round, how can anyone keep the present moment at arm's length?

sentences.zh: 且安有壽之與夭兮，或者情橫多戀。

translations.literal: Moreover, how can there be longevity versus early death, unless feeling runs wild with too many attachments?
translations.idiomatic: What sense is there in calling one span long and another short, except where passion clings too fiercely?

sentences.zh: 宗統竟初不別兮，大德亡其情願。

translations.literal: The ancestral line from start to end is not divided; great virtue forgets its private wishes.
translations.idiomatic: The lineage runs unbroken from root to tip; the greatest virtue is to release private craving.

sentences.zh: 蠢動皆神之為兮，癡聖惟質所建。

translations.literal: The stirring of the dullest creatures is the work of spirit; folly and sageness are both what substance establishes.
translations.idiomatic: Even the twitch of the smallest worm is spirit at work; fool and sage alike are fashioned from the same stuff.

sentences.zh: 真人都遣穢累兮，性茫蕩而無岸。

translations.literal: The perfected person casts off defilement; nature is vast and shoreless.
translations.idiomatic: The perfected man sheds the world's grime, while human nature stretches wide without a farther shore.

sentences.zh: 縱驅於遼廓之庭兮，委體乎寂寥之館。

translations.literal: He gallops in the courtyard of the boundless; he lodges his body in the hall of still silence.
translations.idiomatic: He races through the boundless inner courtyard and rests his frame in the silent, empty lodge.

sentences.zh: 天地短於朝生兮，億代促於始旦。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth are shorter than a mayfly's dawn; a billion ages hurry by before the first light.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth are briefer than a mayfly's morning; aeons flash past before the first dawn breaks.

sentences.zh: 顧瞻宇宙微細兮，眇若豪鋒之半。

translations.literal: Looking back, the cosmos is minute, tiny as half a down-tip.
translations.idiomatic: Glance backward and the universe shrinks to half a speck of down.

sentences.zh: 飄搖玄曠之域兮，深漠暢而靡玩。

translations.literal: Drifting in the realm of dark vastness, profound and desolate, there is nothing to relish.
translations.idiomatic: He drifts in dark immensity—depth without limit, desolation without charm.

sentences.zh: 兀與自然並體兮，融液忽而四散。

translations.literal: Suddenly he merges with spontaneity's body; fused and flowing, in an instant he scatters everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly he shares one body with spontaneity itself, melting and pouring away on every side.

sentences.zh: 」從子亮見賦，問曰：「若有意也，非賦所盡；

translations.literal: His nephew Liang read the rhapsody and asked, "If there is intent, a rhapsody cannot exhaust it;
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Yu Liang read the work and asked, "If you still harbour intent, no poem can exhaust it;

sentences.zh: 若無意也，復何所賦？

translations.literal: if there is no intent, what then is there to rhapsodize?
translations.idiomatic: if you have left intent behind, what is left for a rhapsody to say?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「在有無之間耳！」

translations.literal: He answered, "It lies between having and not having!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ai replied, "Between having intent and having none—that is where I stand!"

sentences.zh: 遷吏部郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 是時天下多故，機變屢起，敳常靜默無為。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was full of troubles; stratagems arose again and again, yet Yu Ai constantly remained silent and non-active.
translations.idiomatic: The age seethed with intrigue and sudden shifts, yet Yu Ai stayed quiet and let events run their course.

sentences.zh: 參東海王越太傅軍事，轉軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: He joined the staff of Prince Sima Yue of Donghai as Grand Mentor, then was transferred Libationer-adviser on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served on Grand Mentor Sima Yue of Donghai's staff, then moved to the post of army libationer.

sentences.zh: 時越府多雋異，敳在其中，常自袖手。

translations.literal: At that time Yue's headquarters teemed with brilliant men; Yu Ai among them often kept his hands in his sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's bureau glittered with talent, yet Yu Ai usually stood apart with folded arms, refusing to jostle for favour.

sentences.zh: 豫州牧長史河南郭象善《老》《莊》，時人以為王弼之亞。

translations.literal: The Chief Clerk of the Governor of Yuzhou, Guo Xiang of Henan, was skilled in the Laozi and Zhuangzi; people of the time considered him second only to Wang Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang of Henan, chief clerk to the governor of Yuzhou, excelled at the 《Laozi》 and 《Zhuangzi》; contemporaries ranked him just below Wang Bi.

sentences.zh: 敳甚知之，每曰：「郭子玄何必減瘐子嵩」。

translations.literal: Yu Ai understood him deeply and often said, "Guo Zixuan need not rank below Yu Zisong."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ai knew his worth and used to say, "Guo Zixuan has nothing to fear beside Yu Zisong."

sentences.zh: 象後為太傅主簿，任事專勢。

translations.literal: Later Guo Xiang became chief clerk to the Grand Mentor, wielding affairs and monopolizing influence.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guo Xiang became chief clerk to the Grand Mentor, running business with a heavy hand.

sentences.zh: 敳謂象曰：「卿自是當世大才，我疇昔之意都已盡矣。」

translations.literal: Yu Ai said to Guo Xiang, "You are indeed a great talent of the age; the regard I once had for you is now exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ai told him plainly, "You are a leading intellect of our day, but the esteem I once felt for you is spent."

sentences.zh: 敳有重名，為搢紳所推，而聚斂積實，談者譏之。

translations.literal: Yu Ai had a weighty reputation and was esteemed by the gentry, yet he amassed wealth; talkers ridiculed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ai enjoyed towering repute among the silk-robed elite, yet he piled up riches, and gossips mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 都官從事溫嶠奏之，敳更器嶠，目嶠森森如千丈松，雖礧砢多節，施之大廈，有棟樑之用。

translations.literal: Director of the capital bureau Wen Jiao reported him; Yu Ai instead came to respect Jiao, describing him as lofty as a thousand-foot pine—though gnarled with many knots, employed in a great hall it has the use of a ridge-beam.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao of the capital bureau denounced him, yet Yu Ai only grew to admire Wen Jiao, likening him to a thousand-foot pine: knotted and rugged, yet the timber you want for a palace ridgepole.

sentences.zh: 時劉輿見任于越，人士多為所構，惟敳縱心事外，無跡可間。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yu was trusted by Sima Yue, and many gentlemen were framed by him; only Yu Ai let his mind roam beyond affairs, leaving no trace by which he could be wedged apart.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu then enjoyed Yue's confidence and ruined many colleagues; only Yu Ai kept his heart outside the fray, offering no foothold for intrigue.

sentences.zh: 後以其性儉家富，說越令就換錢千萬，冀其有吝，因此可乘。

translations.literal: Later, because of his stingy nature and wealthy household, Liu Yu persuaded Yue to summon him to exchange ten million cash, hoping he would be stingy and thereby an opening could be exploited.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Yu Ai was tight-fisted yet rich, Liu Yu talked Yue into ordering him to put up ten million cash for an exchange, expecting miserliness that could be turned against him.

sentences.zh: 越于眾坐中問於敳，而敳乃穨然已醉，幘墮機上，以頭就穿取，徐答-{云}-：「下官家有二千萬，隨公所取矣。

translations.literal: Yue asked Yu Ai about it in the midst of the assembly; Yu Ai was already utterly drunk, his headcloth fell onto the crossbow bench, and he put his head through the hole to retrieve it, slowly saying, "This humble official's household has twenty million; take what you will."
translations.idiomatic: Before the whole company Yue raised the demand. Yu Ai was dead drunk by then—his turban slipped onto the crossbow rack and he fished it back by threading his head through the slit—then drawled, "I keep twenty million at home; help yourself to whatever share you like."

sentences.zh: 」輿於是乃服。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liu Yu was convinced.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu dropped his scheme in admiration.

sentences.zh: 越甚悅，因曰：「不可以小人之慮度君子之心。

translations.literal: Yue was greatly pleased and therefore said, "One must not measure a gentleman's heart with a petty man's thoughts."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue was delighted and remarked, "Never gauge a gentleman's mind with a small man's calculus."

sentences.zh: 」王衍不與敳交，敳卿之不置。

translations.literal: Wang Yan did not associate with Yu Ai, yet Yu Ai doted on him without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan refused his friendship, yet Yu Ai pursued his company relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 衍曰：「君不得為耳。

translations.literal: Yan said, "You simply cannot do it."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan said, "You cannot force this."

sentences.zh: 」敳曰：「卿自君我，我自卿卿。

translations.literal: Yu Ai said, "You may lord it over me as you please; I may dote on you as I please.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Ai shot back, "Call me 'lord' if you wish; I'll still call you darling if I wish."

sentences.zh: 我自用我家法，卿自用卿家法。

translations.literal: I use my family's ways; you use yours.
translations.idiomatic: I follow my family's customs; you follow yours.

sentences.zh: 」衍甚奇之。

translations.literal: Yan greatly marvelled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan could only marvel.

sentences.zh: 石勒之亂，與衍俱被害，時年五十。

translations.literal: During Shi Le's rebellion he perished together with Wang Yan; he was fifty sui at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le rose in revolt, Yu Ai died alongside Wang Yan at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 郭象

translations.literal: Guo Xiang
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang

sentences.zh: 郭象，字子玄，少有才理，好《老》《莊》，能清言。

translations.literal: Guo Xiang, style Zixuan, in youth had talent in reasoning, loved the Laozi and Zhuangzi, and could engage in pure talk.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang, courtesy name Zixuan, showed a sharp logical mind early on, delighted in the 《Laozi》 and 《Zhuangzi》, and shone at *qingtan* debate.

sentences.zh: 太尉王衍每云：「聽象語，如懸河瀉水，注而不竭。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Wang Yan always said, "Listening to Guo Xiang is like a suspended river pouring water—it pours forth without exhaustion."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan used to say, "Hearing Guo Xiang speak is like watching a cataract hang in the air: it floods out and never runs dry."

sentences.zh: 」州郡辟召，不就。

translations.literal: Summons from provinces and commanderies he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He declined every provincial and commandery appointment.

sentences.zh: 常閒居，以文論自娛。

translations.literal: He constantly dwelt in retirement, amusing himself with essays and disquisitions.
translations.idiomatic: He lived quietly at home, passing the time with essays and treatises.

sentences.zh: 後辟司徒掾，稍至黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as retainer to the Minister of Education, and gradually rose to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accepted a retainer's post under the minister of education and worked his way up to gentleman at the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 東海王越引為太傅主簿，甚見親委，遂任職當權，熏灼內外，由是素論去之。

translations.literal: Prince Sima Yue of Donghai drew him in as chief clerk to the Grand Mentor; he was greatly trusted and favoured, then held office and grasped power, scorching within and without; therefore pure opinion turned away from him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue of Donghai made him chief clerk to the Grand Mentor and leaned on him heavily. Guo Xiang soon monopolized power, searing court and camp alike, and men of principle quietly withdrew their respect.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末病卒，著碑論十二篇。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yongjia era he died of illness; he composed twelve stele essays.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at the close of the Yongjia era, leaving twelve commemorative essays.

sentences.zh: 先是，注《莊子》者數十家，莫能究其旨統。

translations.literal: Earlier, those who annotated the Zhuangzi numbered several tens of houses, yet none could exhaust its overarching purport.
translations.idiomatic: Before his day dozens of scholars had glossed the 《Zhuangzi》, yet none had mapped its full design.

sentences.zh: 向秀於舊注外而為解義，妙演奇致，大暢玄風，惟《秋水》、《至樂》二篇未竟而秀卒。

translations.literal: Xiang Xiu, outside the old annotations, composed interpretive meanings, subtly unfolding marvellous reaches and greatly releasing the dark wind; only the chapters Autumn Floods and Perfect Joy he did not finish when Xiu died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiu went beyond older commentaries with a brilliant new reading that opened the text's subtleties and gave new life to Dark Learning—only the 《Autumn Floods》 and 《Perfect Joy》 chapters remained unfinished when he died.

sentences.zh: 秀子幼，其義零落，然頗有別本遷流。

translations.literal: Xiu's son was young; his meanings were scattered, yet there were other copies that circulated.
translations.idiomatic: His son was still a child, so the manuscript fell apart, though stray copies still circulated.

sentences.zh: 象為人行薄，以秀義不傳於世，遂竊以為己注，乃自注《秋水》、《至樂》二篇，又易《馬蹄》一篇，其餘眾篇或點定文句而巳。

translations.literal: Guo Xiang, conduct being shallow, because Xiu's meanings were not transmitted in the world, thereupon stole them to make his own commentary; then he himself annotated Autumn Floods and Perfect Joy, and also altered the chapter Horse's Hoofs; as to the remaining many chapters, he merely dotted and settled sentences and that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang, a man of thin integrity, saw that Xiang Xiu's gloss was not in wide circulation and appropriated it as his own. He added fresh notes only on 《Autumn Floods》 and 《Perfect Joy》, revised 《Horse's Hoofs》, and for the rest merely tweaked wording here and there.

sentences.zh: 其後秀義別本出，故今有向、郭二《莊》，其義一也。

translations.literal: Later Xiu's meanings in a separate copy appeared; therefore today there exist two Zhuangzis, Xiang's and Guo's; their meanings are one.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Xiu's authentic draft resurfaced, the world ended up with two 《Zhuangzi》 traditions—Xiang's and Guo's—though the doctrine is really one.

sentences.zh: 庾純

translations.literal: Yu Chun
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun

sentences.zh: 庾純，字謀甫，博學有才義，為世儒宗。

translations.literal: Yu Chun, style Moufu, was broadly learned and had talent and righteousness; he was the Confucian exemplar of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun, courtesy name Moufu, commanded wide learning, moral clarity, and was revered as the age's leading Confucian.

sentences.zh: 郡補主簿，仍參征南府，累遷黃門侍郎，封關內侯，曆中書令、河南尹。

translations.literal: The commandery appointed him chief clerk; he then joined the staff of the campaign-south headquarters, was repeatedly promoted Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, enfeoffed Marquis Within the Passes, and passed through Palace Secretariat Supervisor and Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery made him chief clerk; he joined the southern campaign staff, rose through gentleman at the Yellow Gates to marquis within the passes, then served as palace secretariat director and governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 初，純以賈充奸佞，與任愷共舉充西鎮關中，充由是不平。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Jia Chong was treacherous and sycophantic, together with Ren Kai he recommended that Chong be sent west to garrison Guanzhong; Chong therefore was not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, seeing Jia Chong's treachery, Yu Chun joined Ren Kai in urging that Chong be posted west to guard Guanzhong—an affront Chong never forgave.

sentences.zh: 充嘗宴朝士，而純後至，充謂曰：「君行常居人前，今何以在後？

translations.literal: Once when Chong feasted court gentlemen and Chun arrived late, Chong said to him, "Your conduct always places you ahead of people; why are you behind today?"
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet Jia Chong gave for courtiers Yu Chun arrived late. Jia needled him, "You usually elbow your way to the front; why drag in last today?"

sentences.zh: 」純曰：「旦有小市井事不了，是以來後。

translations.literal: Chun said, "In the morning I had small market-street business unfinished; therefore I came late."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun answered, "A petty market errand detained me this morning—that is why I am late."

sentences.zh: 」世言純之先嘗有伍伯者，充之先有市魁者，充、純以此相譏焉。

translations.literal: Worldly talk says that in Chun's ancestors there was one who was a market bailiff, and in Chong's ancestors there was one who was a market chief; Chong and Chun on this account mocked each other.
translations.idiomatic: Wits said Yu Chun's forebears had once been market constables while Jia Chong's had been market bosses—barbs the two men now traded openly.

sentences.zh: 充自以位隆望重，意殊不平。

translations.literal: Chong himself, because his position was lofty and his repute heavy, felt especially displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong, puffed up by rank and reputation, fumed more than ever.

sentences.zh: 及純行酒，充不時飲。

translations.literal: When Chun passed the wine, Chong did not drink in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Chun pressed him to drink, Jia Chong refused to lift his cup on cue.

sentences.zh: 純曰：「長者為壽，何敢爾乎！

translations.literal: Chun said, "The elder offers a longevity toast—how dare you be thus!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun snapped, "An elder raises his cup in blessing—how dare you ignore it?"

sentences.zh: 」充曰：「父老不歸供養，將何言也！

translations.literal: Chong said, "If the old father is not returned to for support, what words are there!"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong retorted, "While your aged father goes unsupported at home, what right have you to lecture others?"

sentences.zh: 」純因發怒曰：「賈充！

translations.literal: Chun thereupon flared in anger and said, "Jia Chong!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun's temper broke: "Jia Chong!"

sentences.zh: 天下凶凶，由爾一人。

translations.literal: All-under-Heaven is in turmoil, because of you alone.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is sliding into chaos, and you alone are the cause.

sentences.zh: 」充曰：「充輔佐二世，蕩平巴、蜀，有何罪而天下為之凶凶？

translations.literal: Chong said, "Chong has assisted two reigns and pacified Ba and Shu; what crime is there that All-under-Heaven is in turmoil for him?"
translations.idiomatic: Jia shouted back, "I have served two emperors and crushed Ba and Shu—what crime have I committed to unsettle the realm?"

sentences.zh: 」純曰：「高貴鄉公何在？

translations.literal: Chun said, "Where is the Duke of Gaoguixiang?"
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun answered, "Then where is Duke Cao Mao of Gaoguixiang?"

sentences.zh: 」眾坐因罷。

translations.literal: The seated assembly thereupon broke up.
translations.idiomatic: The guests scattered in silence.

sentences.zh: 充左右欲執純，中護軍羊琇、侍中王濟佑之，因得出。

translations.literal: Chong's attendants wished to seize Chun; Army Protector Yang Xiu and Palace Attendant Wang Ji shielded him, and he was thus able to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong's guards moved to seize Yu Chun, but Army Protector Yang Xiu and Palace Attendant Wang Ji shielded him until he could slip away.

sentences.zh: 充慚怒，上表解職。

translations.literal: Chong, ashamed and angry, submitted a memorial asking to be relieved of office.
translations.idiomatic: Smarting with humiliation, Jia Chong memorialized to resign his posts.

sentences.zh: 純懼，上河南尹、關內侯印綬，上表自劾曰：

translations.literal: Chun, in fear, presented the seals of Governor of Henan and Marquis Within the Passes and submitted a memorial impeaching himself, stating:
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun, frightened, returned the seals of the Henan governorship and his marquisate and filed a self-accusation that read:

sentences.zh: 御史中丞孔恂劾純，請免官。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Censor-in-chief Kong Xun impeached Chun, requesting removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant censor-in-chief Kong Xun indicted Yu Chun and asked that he be cashiered.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「先王崇尊卑之禮，明貴賤之序，著溫克之德，記沈酗之禍，所以光宣道化，示人軌儀也。

translations.literal: An edict stated, "The former kings honoured the rites of high and low, clarified the order of noble and base, recorded the virtue of warmth and restraint, and noted the disaster of sinking in drunkenness—thereby to broadcast the transformation of the Way and show people the model.
translations.idiomatic: The edict intoned: "Ancient kings exalted hierarchy, fixed noble and base in their places, praised self-restraint, and warned against drowning in wine—all to spread the Way and give the realm a mirror."

sentences.zh: 昔廣漢陵慢宰相，獲犯上之刑；

translations.literal: In olden times Guanghan treated the chancellor with contempt and received punishment for offending superiors;
translations.idiomatic: Once a Guanghan man insulted his chancellor and earned the penalty for lèse-majesté;

sentences.zh: 灌夫托醉肆忿，致誅斃之罪。

translations.literal: Guan Fu, relying on drunkenness to vent rage, incurred the crime of execution.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Fu vented drunken spite and paid with his life.

sentences.zh: 純以凡才，備位卿尹，不惟謙敬之節，不忌覆車之戒，陵上無禮，悖言自口，宜加顯黜，以肅朝倫。

translations.literal: Chun, with ordinary talent, occupies the place of minister and governor; he does not think on the rite of modest respect, does not heed the warning of the overturned cart; he is rude to superiors without ritual, reckless words from his mouth—he should be clearly demoted so as to rectify court norms.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun, a man of middling gifts, sits among chief ministers yet spurns humility, ignores the lesson of the overturned cart, insults his betters, and lets reckless words fly from his lips. He should be disgraced in public to restore court decency.

sentences.zh: 」遂免純官。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chun was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 又以純父老不求供養，使據禮典正其臧否。

translations.literal: Also, because Chun's father was old and he did not seek to support him, they ordered that according to ritual canons his right and wrong be determined.
translations.idiomatic: The court added a charge that he failed to care for an aged father and asked the ritual code to judge his guilt.

sentences.zh: 太傅何曾、太尉荀顗、驃騎將軍齊王攸議曰：「凡斷正臧否，宜先稽之禮、律。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor He Zeng, Grand Commandant Xun Yi, and General of Agile Cavalry on the Left Prince Sima You deliberated, saying, "Whenever deciding right and wrong, one should first examine ritual and statute.
translations.idiomatic: Grand tutor He Zeng, grand commandant Xun Yi, and general of agile cavalry Prince Sima You ruled: "Any verdict must rest on ritual and written law."

sentences.zh: 八十者，一子不從政；

translations.literal: At eighty, one son does not serve in government;
translations.idiomatic: "At eighty, one son may stay home from office;"

sentences.zh: 九十者，其家不從政。

translations.literal: At ninety, his household does not serve in government.
translations.idiomatic: at ninety, the whole household may stand aside.

sentences.zh: 新令亦如之。

translations.literal: The new statutes likewise are thus.
translations.idiomatic: The new code says the same.

sentences.zh: 按純父年八十一，兄弟六人，三人在家，不廢侍養。

translations.literal: Examining Chun's father, his years are eighty-one; brothers are six persons, three at home, not ceasing to attend and support.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun's father is eighty-one; of six brothers, three remain at home, so the old man is not left unattended.

sentences.zh: 純不求供養，其於禮、律未有違也。

translations.literal: That Chun does not seek to support them is not yet a violation of ritual and statute.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun's choice not to resign therefore breaks neither ritual nor statute.

sentences.zh: 司空公以純備位卿尹，望其有加於人。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works, because Chun occupies the place of minister and governor, expected that he would be more than other men.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of works noted that Yu Chun sat among chief ministers and ought to set an example above the common run.

sentences.zh: 而純荒醉，肆其忿怒。

translations.literal: Yet Chun, wildly drunk, vented his rage.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yu Chun, blind drunk, spewed insults instead.

sentences.zh: 臣以為純不遠布孝至之行，而近習常人之失，應在譏貶。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that Chun has not widely displayed utmost filial conduct, but has near at hand fallen into the error of ordinary men; he should receive censure and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: We grant he has not shown heroic filial piety, but his lapse is the common human sort and merits censure, not ruin.

sentences.zh: 」司徒石苞議：「純榮官忘親，惡聞格言，不忠不孝，宜除名削爵土。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Shi Bao deliberated: "Chun, honouring office, forgot his kin, hated to hear proper words—disloyal and unfilial; he should be removed from name and stripped of noble rank and fief."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Shi Bao countered: "Yu Chun chose office over parents and scorned good counsel—both unfilial and disloyal. Strip his titles and lands."

sentences.zh: 」司徒西曹掾劉斌議以為：

translations.literal: Western Bureau retainer to the Minister of Education Liu Bin deliberated, holding that:
translations.idiomatic: Western bureau clerk Liu Bin offered yet another opinion:

sentences.zh: 河南功曹史龐劄等表曰：

translations.literal: Functionaries of Henan, clerk Pang Zha and others, submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: Henan clerks led by Pang Zha tabled a joint appeal:

sentences.zh: 帝復下詔曰：「自中世以來，多為貴重順意，賤者生情，故令釋之、定國得揚名於前世。

translations.literal: The Emperor again issued an edict saying, "From middle antiquity onward, many have favoured the noble and weighty who comply with their wishes, while the lowly give rise to feelings; therefore Shi Ji and Yu Dingguo were able to make their names shine in former ages.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spoke again: "Since mid-antiquity judges have often truckled to the mighty while venting spite on the weak—which is how men like Shi Ji and Yu Dingguo won fame by doing justice."

sentences.zh: 今議責庾純，不惟溫克，醉酒沈湎，此責人以齊聖也。

translations.literal: Now, in deliberating blame for Yu Chun, they do not think on restraint; drunkenness and sinking in wine—this is blaming others with the standard of the perfectly sage.
translations.idiomatic: To fault Yu Chun now for lacking perfect sobriety is to demand sagehood of a man reeling at a banquet.

sentences.zh: 疑賈公亦醉，若其不醉，終不於百客之中責以不去官供養也。

translations.literal: I suspect Duke Jia was also drunk; if he were not drunk, in the end he would not, among a hundred guests, reproach him for not leaving office to provide support.
translations.idiomatic: I suspect Duke Jia was drunk himself; had he been sober he would never have raised, before a hundred guests, the charge that Yu Chun refused to quit office to nurse his father.

sentences.zh: 大晉依聖人典禮，制臣子出處之宜，若有八十，皆當歸養，亦不獨純也。

translations.literal: Great Jin, relying on the sages' ritual canons, regulated the proper pattern for subjects' and sons' going forth and staying home; if there is someone eighty, all should return to support him, and it is not Chun alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Jin follows the sages' statutes on when officials may serve or retire: anyone with an eighty-year-old parent ought to go home to care for him, not Yu Chun alone.

sentences.zh: 古人云：'由醉之言，俾出童羖。

translations.literal: The ancients said, 'From the words of the drunkard, make him bring forth the black lamb.
translations.idiomatic: The classic warns: take a drunkard's taunts as seriously as if he demanded you produce a black ram.

sentences.zh: '明不責醉，恐失度也。

translations.literal: 'This clarifies that one does not punish drunkenness, fearing to miss measure.
translations.idiomatic: That means you do not punish mere drunkenness, lest you lose all sense of proportion.

sentences.zh: 所以免純者，當為將來之醉戒耳。

translations.literal: The reason for pardoning Chun should be to take warning for future drunkenness.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun is pardoned precisely so the realm may learn restraint the next time wine flows at court.

sentences.zh: 齊王、劉掾議當矣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi's and Clerk Liu's deliberations were correct.
translations.idiomatic: The opinions of Prince Sima You and clerk Liu Bin were sound.

sentences.zh: 」復以純為國子祭酒，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Again Chun was made Libationer of the National University, with addition of Palace Attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun was reappointed libationer of the National University with the added title of palace attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 後將軍荀眅于朝會中奏純以前坐不孝免黜，不宜升進。

translations.literal: General of the Rear Xun Pan at a court assembly reported that Chun, because of his earlier seat, had been removed for unfilial conduct and ought not be promoted.
translations.idiomatic: At open court General of the Rear Xun Pan memorialized that Yu Chun's earlier dismissal for unfiliality disqualified him from fresh promotion.

sentences.zh: 侍中甄德進曰：「孝以顯親為大，祿養為榮。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-ordinary Zhen De advanced, saying, "Filial piety takes making one's parents illustrious as great, and salary nurture as honour.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Zhen De rose to argue: "True filial piety means bringing glory to one's parents and supporting them on official income."

sentences.zh: 詔赦純前愆，擢為近侍，兼掌教官，此純召不俟駕之日。

translations.literal: The edict pardoned Chun's former fault, raised him to be a close attendant, and also charged him with instructing officers—this is the day when Chun, summoned, did not wait for the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The throne had already forgiven Yu Chun's slip, elevated him as an inner-court adviser, and entrusted him with the education of cadets—the very model of a subject who answered a summons without waiting for his carriage.

sentences.zh: 而後將軍眅敢以私議貶奪公論，抗言矯情，誣罔朝廷，宜加貶黜。

translations.literal: Yet General of the Rear Pan dared, with private opinion, to belittle public consensus, speak confrontationally with feigned righteousness, and deceive the court; he should receive demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xun Pan presumed to use private spite to overturn a settled consensus, posturing as righteous while slandering the court—he deserves demotion.

sentences.zh: 」眅坐免官。

translations.literal: Pan by seat was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Pan was stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 初，眅與純俱為大將軍所辟，眅整麗車服，純率素而已，眅以為愧恨。

translations.literal: Earlier, Pan and Chun were both summoned by the Grand General; Pan adorned his carriage and robes neatly, while Chun was plain and simple only; Pan therefore felt shame and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Xun Pan and Yu Chun had both been recruited by the grand general: Xun Pan arrived in glossy equipage while Yu Chun came plainly dressed, and Xun Pan nursed a grudge for the contrast.

sentences.zh: 至是，毀純。

translations.literal: When it came to this, he slandered Chun.
translations.idiomatic: He now used the affair to smear Yu Chun.

sentences.zh: 眅既免黜，純更以此愧之，亟往慰勉之，時人稱純通恕。

translations.literal: After Pan was dismissed, Chun on this account felt ashamed for him and repeatedly went to console and encourage him; people of the time praised Chun as magnanimous.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xun Pan fell, Yu Chun was ashamed on his behalf and visited him again and again to cheer him up; contemporaries praised Yu Chun's breadth of mind.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，以父憂去官。

translations.literal: He was promoted Palace Attendant; because of mourning for his father he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to palace attendant but stepped down to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 起為御史中丞，轉尚書。

translations.literal: He was raised up as Palace Attendant Censor-in-chief, then transferred to Director in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as palace attendant censor-in-chief, then moved to director in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 除魏郡太守，不之官，拜少府。

translations.literal: He was appointed Administrator of Wei commandery; he did not go to the post, and was appointed Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was named governor of Wei commandery but never took up the post, receiving instead the ministership of the household.

sentences.zh: 年六十四卒。

translations.literal: At age sixty-four he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 子旉。

translations.literal: His son was Fu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yu Fu.

translations.literal: The transmitted line consists of an equals sign with no lexical gloss in the edition used here.
translations.idiomatic: The edition again inserts a lone equals sign, almost certainly a table-row artifact.

sentences.zh: 子旉

translations.literal: Son Fu
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fu

sentences.zh: =旉字允臧。

translations.literal: Yu Fu, style Yuncang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fu, courtesy name Yuncang—the stray mark before his name is an edition artifact.

sentences.zh: 少有清節，歷位博士。

translations.literal: In youth he had pure integrity; he passed through the post of erudit.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was known for spotless conduct and rose through a doctorate.

sentences.zh: 齊王攸之就國也，下禮官議崇錫之物。

translations.literal: When Prince Sima You of Qi went to his state, an order was issued to ritual officials to deliberate on the objects of honour and grants.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Sima You of Qi prepared to leave for his fief, the court ordered the ritual bureau to decide what honours and gifts to bestow.

sentences.zh: 旉與博士太叔廣、劉暾、繆蔚、郭頤、秦秀、傅珍等上表諫曰：

translations.literal: Fu together with erudits Taishu Guang, Liu Tun, Miao Wei, Guo Yi, Qin Xiu, Fu Zhen, and others submitted a memorial remonstrating, stating:
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fu joined erudits Taishu Guang, Liu Tun, Miao Wei, Guo Yi, Qin Xiu, Fu Zhen, and others in a memorial of remonstrance that read:

sentences.zh: 旉草議，先以呈父純，純不禁。

translations.literal: Fu drafted the deliberation and first presented it to his father Chun; Chun did not forbid him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fu drafted the protest and showed it to his father Yu Chun, who raised no objection.

sentences.zh: 太常鄭默、博士祭酒曹志並過其事。

translations.literal: Chamberlain of Ceremonies Zheng Mo and Libationer Cao Zhi both passed by the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Chamberlain Zheng Mo and Libationer Cao Zhi were likewise drawn into the business.

sentences.zh: 武帝以博士不答所問，答所不問，大怒，事下有司。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, because the erudits did not answer what was asked but answered what was not asked, was greatly angry, and the matter was handed to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, furious that the scholars answered beside the point, referred the case to the bureaus.

sentences.zh: 尚書硃整、褚䂮等奏：「旉等侵官離局，迷罔朝廷，崇飾惡言，假託無諱，請收旉等八人付廷尉科罪。

translations.literal: Director Zhu Zheng, Chu Li, and others memorialized: "Fu and the others encroached on offices and departed from their jurisdiction, misled the court, adorned vile language, and falsely pretended to lack restraint; we request that Fu and eight others be seized and handed to the Commandant of Justice for sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: Directors Zhu Zheng and Chu Li reported that Yu Fu and his colleagues had exceeded their brief, confused the throne, and peddled slander thinly veiled as frankness, and asked that Yu Fu and seven others be sent to the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 」旉父純詣廷尉自首：「旉以議草見示，愚淺聽之。

translations.literal: Fu's father Chun went to the Commandant of Justice and surrendered himself, saying, "Fu showed me the draft deliberation; in folly and shallowness I listened.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chun appeared at the Commandant of Justice and confessed: "My son showed me his draft; I listened like a fool."

sentences.zh: 」詔免純罪。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned Chun's crime.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor forgave Yu Chun.

sentences.zh: 廷尉劉頌又奏旉等大不敬，棄市論，求平議。

translations.literal: Commandant of Justice Liu Song again memorialized that Fu and the others were guilty of great irreverence, with judgment of execution in the marketplace, requesting a balanced deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Liu Song renewed the charge of grave lèse-majesté against Yu Fu and company, recommending public execution pending a full collegial review.

sentences.zh: 尚書又奏請報聽廷尉行刑。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing again memorialized requesting approval to let the Commandant carry out the sentence.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing asked leave to let the commandant enforce the death verdict.

sentences.zh: 尚書夏侯駿謂硃整曰：「國家乃欲誅諫臣！

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Xiahou Jun said to Zhu Zheng, "The state intends to execute remonstrating ministers!
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Jun of the Masters of Writing told Zhu Zheng, "The court would kill men for daring to remonstrate!"

sentences.zh: 官立八座，正為此時，卿可共駁正之。

translations.literal: The court established eight seats precisely for such a moment; you can together refute and correct it.
translations.idiomatic: Those eight senior seats exist for exactly such crises—you must join me in blocking this.

sentences.zh: 」整不從，駿怒起，曰：「非所望也！

translations.literal: Zheng did not comply; Jun angrily rose and said, "This is not what I expected of you!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zheng refused. Xiahou Jun rose in fury and said, "Then I expected too much of you!"

sentences.zh: 」乃獨為駁議。

translations.literal: Thereupon he alone composed a refuting deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore drafted a lone rebuttal.

sentences.zh: 左僕射魏舒、右僕射下邳王晃等從駿議。

translations.literal: Left Director Wei Shu, Right Director Prince Sima Huang of Xiapi, and others followed Jun's deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Left director Wei Shu, right director Prince Sima Huang of Xiapi, and the rest sided with Xiahou Jun.

sentences.zh: 奏留中七日，乃詔曰：「旉等備為儒官，不念奉憲制，不指答所問，敢肆其誣罔之言，以幹亂視聽。

translations.literal: The memorial was detained in the palace seven days; then an edict stated, "Fu and the others, filling Confucian offices, did not think to uphold statutes, did not pointedly answer what was asked, and dared to unleash deceitful words to disturb what is seen and heard.
translations.idiomatic: After a week the emperor ruled: "Yu Fu and his fellow scholars ignored the law, evaded the question, and spread lies that poisoned public opinion."

sentences.zh: 而旉是議主，應為戮首。

translations.literal: Yet Fu was chief author of the deliberation and should be chief among those executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fu led the memorial and should bear the heaviest blame.

sentences.zh: 但旉及家人並自首，大信不可奪。

translations.literal: But Fu and his family all surrendered themselves; great trust cannot be wrested away.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yu Fu and his kin had all confessed in person, and imperial good faith must not be broken.

sentences.zh: 秦秀、傅珍前者虛妄，幸而得免，復不以為懼，當加罪戮，以彰凶慝。

translations.literal: Qin Xiu and Fu Zhen earlier were false and vain, luckily were pardoned, yet again did not take it as warning; they should receive punishment and execution to display viciousness.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xiu and Fu Zhen had already escaped once for empty rhetoric; fear taught them nothing and they deserve added punishment to expose malice.

sentences.zh: 猶復不忍，皆丐其死命。

translations.literal: Still We cannot bear it and all beg for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Still I cannot bring myself to kill them outright.

sentences.zh: 秀、珍、旉等並除名。

translations.literal: Xiu, Zhen, Fu, and the rest were all removed from name.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xiu, Fu Zhen, Yu Fu, and the others were stricken from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 」後數歲，復起為散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: After several years he was again raised as Palace Attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Yu Fu was recalled as palace attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 終於國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He ended as Libationer of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as libationer of the National University.

sentences.zh: 秦秀

translations.literal: Qin Xiu
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xiu

sentences.zh: 秦秀，字玄良，新興雲中人也。

translations.literal: Qin Xiu, style Xuanliang, was a man of Yunzhong in Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xiu, courtesy name Xuanliang, came from Yunzhong in Xinxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 父朗，魏驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: His father Lang was Wei General of Agile Cavalry on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qin Lang had served Wei as general of agile cavalry on the right.

sentences.zh: 秀少敦學行，以忠直知名。

translations.literal: Xiu in youth was earnest in study and conduct, and was known for loyalty and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Qin Xiu studied diligently and was famed for blunt integrity.

sentences.zh: 咸甯中，為博士。

translations.literal: In the Xianning era he was an erudit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianning era he held a doctorate.

sentences.zh: 何曾卒，下禮官議諡。

translations.literal: When He Zeng died, an order went to ritual officials to deliberate on his posthumous name.
translations.idiomatic: When He Zeng died, the court asked the ritualists for a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 秀議曰：

translations.literal: Xiu deliberated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xiu argued:

sentences.zh: 故太宰何曾，雖階世族之胤，而少以高亮嚴肅，顯登王朝。

translations.literal: The former Grand Tutor He Zeng, though a descendant of a hereditary great clan, in youth by high brightness and sternness plainly ascended the royal court.
translations.idiomatic: The late grand tutor He Zeng, though born to privilege, first rose through conspicuous dignity and austerity.

sentences.zh: 事親有色養之名，在官奏科尹模，此二者實得臣子事上之概。

translations.literal: In serving parents he had a name for "colour nurture"; in office he memorialized to impeach Yin Mo—these two indeed grasp the outline of how subjects serve superiors.
translations.idiomatic: He won praise for delighting his parents at table and once impeached the minister Yin Mo—both deeds show the heart of a loyal servant.

sentences.zh: 然資性驕奢，不循軌則。

translations.literal: Yet his endowed nature was arrogant and extravagant; he did not follow tracks and norms.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his temperament was arrogant and spendthrift, heedless of proper bounds.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「節彼南山，惟石岩岩，赫赫師尹，人具爾瞻。
